  "thinking": "Leo's sketched a sitting fox, which is what I wanted. Priya is the only holdout and her worry was the blob risk, so I'll address that directly and ask her to align. Nothing can be built until she does.",
  "say": "Fair point on the blob, Priya. So let's not curl it up. Leo's sitting fox is what I had in mind: two sharp ears, a long snout, the tail swept out to the side. It stays readable even if a few dominoes miss, it's still calm and wise, and it ties to the owner's favourite book, so I think the client will be happy. Can you live with it? If so, say aligned and we can get going. Leo, nice sketch. Keep going, maybe make the tail a bit bigger and fluffier so it clearly says fox and not dog.",
  "to": "everyone",
  "eagerness": 7,
  "do": "stop",
  "aligned": "fox",
  "notes": "Client: kids bookshop window, calm and wise, friendly and at rest, no owls, no cat (Biscuit), owner's favourite book is about a fox. Plan: upright sitting fox (not curled, to avoid a blob) with pointy ears, snout, big bushy tail. I'm aligned on fox, so are Tom and Leo. Waiting on Priya (elephant). Leo holds the pad and has sketched a sitting fox. Once everyone is aligned, someone traces stroke 1 from START, then I trace the other strokes."
